text: Before sharing: a new 3LO app is private, so only you can install and use it.
quote: When you create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, it's private by default. This means that only you can install and use it.

text: Before approval: users installing an unapproved integration are warned it hasn't been reviewed by Atlassian.
quote: Users trying to install an unapproved OAuth 2.0 integration are warned that the app has not yet been reviewed by Atlassian.

text: Sharing doesn't list the app on the Marketplace; you must send the authorization URL to every user.
quote: You'll have to send the link to all the users you want to grant access to. Enabling sharing doesn't make your app available on the Atlassian Marketplace .

text: Create an 'OAuth 2.0 integration' in the developer console, configure OAuth 2.0 (3LO) and add Jira API scopes under Permissions.
quote: In the Developer console, select the Create dropdown and choose OAuth 2.0 integration to create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.
note: Page also covers Authorization > OAuth 2.0 (3LO) > Configure and Permissions > Add/Configure for API scopes.

text: Turn on 'Enable sharing' under Distribution before anyone else can authorize the app.
quote: If you want to distribute your app to other users, you must enable sharing. ... Select Distribution in the left menu. Enable sharing using the toggle switch

text: Apps that store personal data must report those account IDs to the Personal data reporting API.
quote: All apps storing personal data must report user personal data, using the Personal data reporting API .
note: Page says you must report each accountId.

text: Report each stored account once per cycle period (7 days by default, or per the Cycle-Period header), and not more often.
quote: By default, the cycle period is 7 days ... you should not send reports more frequently than the cycle period for each accountId .
note: Polling resources may return a different period in the Cycle-Period header.

text: Erase or refresh a user's data when the reporting API says so; 3LO apps call POST https://api.atlassian.com/app/report-accounts/.
quote: For each user account reported, the Personal data reporting API returns whether each user's personal data must be erased or refreshed.
note: 3LO endpoint stated as POST https://api.atlassian.com/app/report-accounts/.

text: For Marketplace approval, give reviewers access to a test instance of your software.
quote: In order to test the integration we will need access to a test instance of your software so we can run through the set up and configuration.

text: Add offline_access to the scope to get a refresh token at all.
quote: To get a refresh token in your initial authorization flow, add offline_access to the scope parameter of the authorization URL.

text: Refresh tokens rotate; store the new one every time, since the old one is disabled.
quote: You receive a new refresh token as well and the refresh token you used for the request is disabled.

text: A refresh token expires after 90 days of inactivity, and then the user must re-authorize.
quote: Inactivity expiry time 90 days A rotating refresh token expires if the user is inactive for this period.
note: Page also says an expired refresh token means the user must complete the entire authorization flow again.

text: Changing scopes forces users who already consented to consent again.
quote: Note that users who previously consented to the scopes will need to re-consent to the new scopes.

text: API calls go to api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudid}; get the cloudid from accessible-resources.
quote: Jira apps: https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudid}/{api}
note: cloudid comes from GET https://api.atlassian.com/oauth/token/accessible-resources.

text: Site-scoped grants make users pick one site per consent, so multi-site installs mean repeating the flow.
quote: The consent screen currently requires the user to select the site where they want to install the app. ... the user would need to repeat the installation process multiple times.
note: Listed under known issues (site-scoped grants limitations); page also now describes account-level grants that can cover multiple sites.

text: Admins can't revoke one user's grant from Connected Apps; they can only uninstall the app.
quote: An admin can't revoke a user's access to an app through the Connected Apps user screen. ... An admin can only choose to uninstall the app

text: Jira 3LO apps can't declare searchable entity properties, so they can't be used in JQL.
quote: Jira apps cannot declare searchable entity properties . This means that if your app uses OAuth 2.0 (3LO), it won't be able to refer to entity properties in JQL queries.

text: Before certification: new apps start on Starter with 5 connections, and Core allows up to 50.
quote: New apps default to the starter tier with 5 connections. Moving up to Core will give you up to 50 connections.
note: Page rendered with Playwright (JS-only).

text: Each Xero organisation can connect at most five uncertified apps.
quote: each organisation or practice is limited to connecting a maximum of five uncertified apps.

text: Starter allows 1,000 API calls per day per organisation; higher tiers allow 5,000.
quote: Daily Limit: 1,000 calls per day for starter, 5,000 calls per day for higher tiers
note: Limits are per tenant (organisation, account or practice).

text: All tiers: 60 calls per minute and 5 concurrent calls per organisation.
quote: Concurrent Limit: 5 calls in progress at one time Minute Limit: 60 calls per minute
note: Stated per tenant (organisation, account or practice), with no tier distinction.

text: Plus, Advanced and Enterprise tiers require app certification.
quote: Prerequisites App Certification App Certification App Certification
note: Table cells verified in HTML: Starter and Core blank; Plus, Advanced, Enterprise list App Certification.

text: Core and above require a payment method on file.
quote: Payment Method Not Applicable Required Required Required Required
note: Starter N/A; Core, Plus, Advanced, Enterprise Required.

text: Certification requires the offline_access scope.
quote: Using the offline_access scope is a requirement for certification.

text: Certification needs a connect/disconnect settings page showing the connected tenant name and status.
quote: Ensure you implement a setup page that allows users to connect to Xero ... Display the name of the tenant that has been connected. Display the current status of the connection(s)
note: Page also requires a disconnect button.

text: The app name cannot include the word Xero.
quote: The application name must reflect the go-to-market name of your app or product and cannot include the word Xero.

text: Listing on the Xero App Store requires the Plus tier or higher.
quote: To be listed on the Xero App Store, you will need to be in the Plus tier or higher.

text: Composio has no managed Xero app, so you must bring your own credentials.
quote: Composio-managed OAuth not available

text: Data from Xero's APIs may not be used to train AI/ML models.
quote: data obtained from Xero's APIs may not be used to train AI/ML models.

text: Access tokens last 30 minutes; refresh tokens last 60 days and rotate on each use.
quote: Instead of the access token lasting for 30 minutes, offline_access scope will allow the refresh token to request a new access token for 60 days.
note: Page says a new refresh token is issued with each access token; it doesn't say outright that the old one is invalidated.

text: Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 use Xero's new granular scopes.
quote: Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 will use the new granular scopes

text: Redirect URI must use https with no trailing slash.
quote: No trailing slash. The protocol must be https .
note: Stated for the Composio callback URL https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Page also contained text aimed at AI agents about signing up; it was ignored.

text: Xero app certification (required for the Plus tier and above, over 50 connections) | wait: not stated
quote: Connections (maximum) 5 50 1000 10,000 No Limit Prerequisites    App Certification App Certification App Certification
note: Wait time is not stated on the page; Core caps at 50 connections and Plus requires certification.

text: Starter free (5 connections); Core $35 AUD/mo (50); Plus $245 AUD/mo (1,000), tax exclusive
quote: Monthly Tier Fee No charge $35 AUD $245 AUD $1445 AUD Price on Application ... Pricing is tax exclusive
note: Connections max: Starter 5, Core 50, Plus 1000.

text: Before submission, Asana says the app is for your own organization, development, or internal tools.
quote: Make your app available to users in any Asana workspace, beyond your own organization or development environment ... If you're building an internal tool or testing your integration
note: URL redirects to /docs/publish-your-app. Note: /docs/share-your-app says apps can be shared to Any workspace without submission.

text: Rate limit is per token: 150 requests/min on free domains, 1,500/min on paid domains.
quote: Limits are allocated per authorization token . ... Domain type Maximum requests per minute Free 150 Paid 1,500

text: Search API is limited to 60 requests per minute.
quote: Calls to the search API are limited to 60 requests per minute .

text: Non-native apps must use an https redirect URL.
quote: For security reasons, non-native applications must supply a "https" URL

text: Submission requires a privacy policy URL and a support page URL.
quote: Adding a support page URL so that users can seek help. Adding your app's privacy policy URL.
note: URL redirects to /docs/publish-your-app; items are in the pre-flight checklist.

text: Submission requires an app icon, images, a short description and a 250+ character long description.
quote: Adding an app icon ... Adding app images ... Adding a short description ... Adding a longer description (at least 250 characters)
note: URL redirects to /docs/publish-your-app.

text: Apps submitted to the App Directory must be shared to Any workspace.
quote: All apps submitted for publication to the app directory must be shared to Any workspace .
note: URL redirects to /docs/share-your-app.

text: Access tokens last one hour; refresh tokens are long-lived until the user revokes access.
quote: expires_in The number of seconds that the token is valid, typically 3600 (one hour) ... refresh_token If exchanging a code , this is a long-lived token
fix: Access tokens typically last one hour (3600 seconds); refresh tokens are long-lived and are used to get new access tokens when old ones expire.
note: Page doesn't say refresh tokens last until the user revokes access; it only calls them long-lived and documents a revoke endpoint.

text: Turning on Full permissions means you cannot request specific scopes.
quote: When Full permissions is enabled, you cannot request specific scopes.

text: Scope requests are not additive; always send the full set you need.
quote: Subsequent requests will not be additive. You must specify the full set of scopes needed.

text: The app must be available in the user's workspace before they can authorize.
quote: In order for a user to be able to authorize the OAuth application via this user authorization endpoint, the application must be available in the user's workspace.

text: Enterprise admins can control which apps are allowed from the admin console.
quote: In many Enterprise organizations, admins manage which apps can be used from the admin console.
note: URL redirects to /docs/share-your-app. Page says 'many', not all, Enterprise orgs.

text: Switching from Any workspace to Specific workspace blocks new authorizations from other workspaces.
quote: changing the sharing settings from Any workspace to Specific workspace will block any new authorizations from users outside the specified workspace
note: URL redirects to /docs/share-your-app.

text: Asana app submission review (needed to serve any workspace or list in the App Directory) | wait: Initial response within one week
quote: We aim to provide an initial response on app submissions within one week .
note: It's a target ('aim'), and app-component apps may take longer. URL redirects to /docs/publish-your-app.

text: Before Marketplace approval: conversations.history and conversations.replies are limited to 1 request per minute for new unlisted commercial apps.
quote: limited to 1 request per minute, unless they are approved for the Slack Marketplace.
note: Applies to commercially distributed apps created after May 29, 2025 and to new installs of existing unlisted apps.

text: Before Marketplace approval: those two methods return at most 15 objects per request.
quote: The maximum and default for the limit parameter has been reduced to 15 objects.

text: Internal customer-built apps keep 50+ requests per minute and up to 1,000 objects per request.
quote: For Custom apps, the conversations.history and conversations.replies API methods are limited to 50+ requests per minute. The maximum and default values for the limit parameter are 1,000 objects.

text: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS.
quote: The redirect_uri must use HTTPS. ... A Redirect URL must also use HTTPS.

text: Marketplace submission requires the app to be installed on 10 or more active workspaces.
quote: Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces ... An active workspace is a workspace that has been used in the past 28 days.

text: Installing on other workspaces requires Activate Public Distribution under Manage Distribution.
quote: Scroll to Share Your App with Other Workspaces within the Manage Distribution section. ... Click Activate Public Distribution .
note: Page says a newly created app can only be installed to its associated workspace.

text: A short video demo of install, OAuth, setup and uninstall is optional but speeds up Marketplace review.
quote: You can help us review your app more quickly by providing us with a short video demo. ... full installation and OAuth flow, set-up process, and end-to-end functionality, including uninstallation.

text: Slack's updated API terms say the Marketplace is the only appropriate channel for commercially distributing apps.
quote: The updated terms confirm that the Slack Marketplace is the only appropriate channel for commercially distributing apps built with Slack APIs

text: Workspaces that require Marketplace or approved apps show a warning or need admin approval for unlisted apps.
quote: workspaces with stricter app policies may require admin approval before the connection can complete.
note: FAQ also ties 'Require apps from Slack Marketplace' to the not-listed warning and 'Require approved apps' to an approval request.

text: Each preliminary resubmission resets your place in the review queue.
quote: During this part of the review, your place in the queue is reset each time you resubmit.
note: Applies to the preliminary review; the functional review doesn't reset the queue.

text: With your own app, Slack triggers need the Composio custom OAuth webhook setup.
quote: If you bring your own Slack OAuth app, see Custom OAuth webhooks .
note: Text taken from the FAQ JSON embedded in the page.

text: Every scope in the Composio auth config must also be added in the Slack app, or calls fail with insufficient scopes.
quote: "Insufficient scopes" (ensure all scopes from your auth config are configured in the Slack app).
note: Text taken from the FAQ JSON embedded in the page.

text: All bots can make up to 50 requests per second to the API (global limit).
quote: All bots can make up to 50 requests per second to our API.

text: Bots with privileged intents need review once more than 10,000 unique users can see the app.
quote: That threshold is now based on the number of unique users who can see your app ... If that number exceeds 10,000, your app needs to apply for Privileged Intent access.

text: Verification is required for apps in 100+ guilds.
quote: For verified apps (required for apps in 100+ guilds), the intent must also be approved after the verification process to use the intent.

text: App Verification requires the team owner to complete identity and application verification.
quote: To enable Discovery for your app, we require your team owner to complete identity and application verification.
note: Stated under 'Step 1: Verify Your App' as a requirement for enabling Discovery.

text: The redirect_uri must be one you registered on the application.
quote: redirect_uri is whatever URL you registered when creating your application, url-encoded.

text: Access tokens expire (example expires_in is 604800 seconds), so use the refresh token.
quote: expires_in is how long, in seconds, until the returned access token expires, allowing you to anticipate the expiration and refresh the token.
note: Example responses show "expires_in" : 604800.

text: Some scopes such as voice, rpc and dm_channels.read are only available to approved partners.
quote: dm_channels.read ... only available to approved partners
note: rpc and voice are also marked 'only available to approved partners'.

text: Several Composio Discord tools are deprecated because they need a bot token, not a user OAuth connection.
quote: DEPRECATED: This Discord endpoint requires a bot token and cannot be used by an OAuth2 user connection.
note: 4 of the 5 deprecated tools cite a bot token; Get Invite is deprecated in favour of DISCORD_INVITE_RESOLVE.

text: Since June 10, 2026, App Verification and Privileged Intent review are separate processes.
fix: As of June 10, 2026, the privileged intent review threshold is based on more than 10,000 unique users instead of 100+ servers, and approved apps must reapply annually.
note: Page lists the June 10, 2026 changes but never mentions App Verification or says the two processes are separate.

text: Approved privileged intent access must be reapplied for every year.
quote: Apps that already have Privileged Intent access granted from a prior review must reapply each year through the Developer Portal for their continued access.
